question: What will the National Bank of Poland's EUR/PLN reference rate be on 13 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Random-walk anchor at latest NBP fixing 4.4185 (2 Nov 2026), 8 trading days to 13 Nov (11 Nov holiday). Zloty at weakest since Dec 2023 after 30 Oct Constitutional Tribunal takeover attempt; added pressure from Glapinski State Tribunal vote (17-19 Nov), US midterms, Iran tensions; offsets: weak USD, possible hawkish MPC 3-4 Nov tone, bank forecasts/forwards pointing to recovery toward ~4.30 by Dec. Median shaded slightly below the spot fix for mild mean reversion against momentum. Market check: harness candidates (Manifold 1000 PLN note, Polymarket SNB) do not match; no EUR/PLN market found.

calls.reasoning: Random-walk anchor at the latest NBP fix of 4.4185 (2 Nov 2026), with 8 fixings left before 13 Nov. Political risk is upward pressure: the Glapinski State Tribunal case (Sejm vote 17-19 Nov), the Constitutional Tribunal clash, the deficit and Moody's downgrade, and EM risk aversion. Against that are bank forecasts of recovery toward ~4.30, repeated recent pullbacks from ~4.41, and an MPC member's talk of a hike above 4.50 acting as a soft cap. These roughly offset, so the median is 4.415, just below the spot fix, with a slight right tail. No human market prices EUR/PLN; the harness candidates (Manifold banknote, Polymarket SNB) do not match.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: the 2 Nov fix is 4.4185, 8 fixings remain (11 Nov is a holiday), daily SD is ~0.3%, the Sejm vote falls after the resolution date, and no matching market exists. Run 3's count of 9 trading days includes 2 Nov itself, so it is not a real conflict. The remaining differences are judgment calls: a slight median shade for mean reversion, and escape mass of 0-1%. With no web access on this run, I re-derived the spread from the shared daily-vol figure (~0.096, widened to ~0.105) and took a median slightly below spot. I agree with the runs' reference class and dispersion basis. A move above 4.60 needs +4.1% in 8 days, so I priced it at 0.5%.
